transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-12 16:30 UTC | Duration: ~46m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark, Lina, Sam, Ravi

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we can start in a minute. Good to meet the CedarMill team. Quick intro, I'm Alex Morgan, AE at Redwood Inference. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. Diego from CS is also on for follow-up.

[00:18] Mark: Hi all, Mark here. Thanks for fitting us in. We're interested in improving our site search relevance and looking at embeddings + rerank as a pilot.

[00:26] Priya: Awesome. We'll walk through the hosted API flow — embeddings for retrieval and a reranker step with the hosted rerank endpoint. I'll also show Console quick configs and Optimize suggestions for batching/quant profiles.

[00:40] Lina: Quick note — security is a must, we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS support for keys. Also data residency for EU queries — most traffic is NA but some EU.

[00:52] Alex: Totally. Happy to share our SOC2 report and KMS integrations. Hosted keeps customer data isolated per account and we have region controls. We'll include that in the follow-up packet.

[01:05] Sam: One question up front — latency. Our SLAs are 100 ms p50 for search rerank end-to-end in the critical path. How realistic is that with hosted?

[01:15] Priya: Good question. p50 100ms is aggressive for a two-step retrieval+rerank depending on model sizes and batch behavior. For a hosted single-pass rerank with a smaller cross-encoder quantized model, we've seen p50s in the 80–150ms range for short queries under typical load. For heavy peak bursts we'd recommend a dedicated or reserved capacity, or use our smart routing to fallback to a lighter-weight variant.

[01:45] Mark: So, hosted + some model variant fallback could work. Cost is also a concern. We run ~1.5M queries/day during peak.

[01:55] Alex: Right. That's where Redwood Optimize helps — it suggests batching levels, quantization (we recommend 4-bit for many cross-encoders), and prefix caching for repeated query shapes to reduce token compute. We'll show the Optimize panel in Console.

[02:12] Priya: Quick agenda: (1) API demo — embeddings + rerank call flow, (2) Console — per-route dashboards, cost/latency breakdown, Optimize suggestions, (3) Pilot plan and benchmarks.

[02:25] Priya: I'll screen-share now. (shared) First, simple retrieval flow: call embeddings endpoint -> store vectors in whichever vector DB -> kNN retrieval -> send top-K candidates into rerank endpoint using text + candidate context. Here's the API snippet we use.

[02:45] Priya: Note: our rerank endpoint supports both a cross-encoder prompt wrapper and function-calling style structured outputs. You can return a score field or a full annotated result.

[03:02] Ravi: Are there SDKs for batch upload of vectors and incremental upserts? Our pipeline is in Python.

[03:10] Priya: Yes, we have Python and Node SDKs. For large upserts we recommend the bulk embeddings endpoint with streaming and then background index building on the DB side. We show an example notebook in the repo.

[03:28] Lina: On the reranker, how do you avoid hallucination when promoting a long document? We need factual matching to product SKUs.

[03:36] Priya: Rerankers are trained to score relevance; they shouldn't hallucinate content into the response since they only score provided candidates. For generation tasks we couple with grounding. For SKU matching, we encourage token-level prefixes and stronger retrieval recall. Also run thresholding and tie-break heuristics in the post-process.

[03:55] Mark: What about the KV cache you mentioned in docs — does that help reuse decoder state? Not sure if it matters for rerank.

[04:02] Priya: The KV cache helps for generation-heavy workloads to avoid recomputation across tokens — not as relevant for cross-encoder rerankers because they process the full text in one forward pass. For multi-turn chat it's a bigger benefit. Sometimes the docs say K V cache which is transcribed oddly.

[04:18] Alex: (laughs) Fireflies loves the K V cache spell outs.

[04:24] Priya: Moving to Console — per-route dashboards show token-level cost, average latency, and a breakdown by model variant. Here's an example of a rerank route configured: concurrency limits, batching window, and fallback policy to a cheaper model if the p50 exceeds X ms.

[04:45] Sam: Can we set a hard latency SLO that triggers fallback automatically? We don't want producers to see errors during spikes.

[04:52] Priya: Yes — you can configure latency SLOs per route and automatic fallback rules. There's also trimming of contexts and autoscaling policies. For hosted we provide autoscaling with burst capacity, though Dedicated gives tighter guarantees.

[05:12] Mark: On data residency, can we pin the tenant to eu-west-1 region for EU queries?

[05:19] Alex: Yes — we can route by policy and region. For hybrid scenarios customers use Private to keep everything on-prem, but for most EU residency needs our hosted regions are sufficient. We'll include the region controls doc.

[05:32] Priya: Now I'll run through a live example with a short query set from an anonymized sample. (runs demo) First the embedding vector call — returns 1536-d vector — small variations depending on model. Then kNN returns top 8 candidates. We pass those to rerank and ask for a score and explanation field.

[06:02] (small pause while demo runs)

[06:14] Priya: You can see the reranker score distribution. For items with strong SKU matches the ranker pushes them to the top. For ambiguous queries it uses contextual cues.

[06:26] Ravi: The explanations look a bit loose — can we get more deterministic signals? We have business rules that must be applied on top.

[06:34] Priya: Totally. We recommend running a rule-based post-filter after rerank, or using the annotated fields to apply rules server-side. Also you can tune the reranker with a small fine-tune or calibrate thresholds via the Console experiments feature.

[06:52] Alex: On calibrating, Redwood Optimize suggests quant/profile combos by analyzing token distributions and suggests a cheaper variant for tail queries. For your traffic profile that could reduce costs ~20-40%.

[07:06] Mark: Do you support client-side SSO provisioning and role-based access in Console? We need RBAC for multiple teams.

[07:12] Priya: Yes — SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC roles. Audit logs are available and can be streamed to your SIEM via webhooks or secure export.

[07:24] Sam: For encryption, does hosted let us use customer-managed keys (CMK)?

[07:29] Alex: Yes — we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for Private. On hosted you can register a CMK and keys are used for at-rest encryption of any customer-specific artifacts. We'll send the KMS integration guide.

[07:41] Lina: For the pilot, we'd like a simple success metric: lift in click-through rate (CTR) for top-3 results by at least 8% and p50 latency under 200ms for rerank. Feels like a realistic target.

[07:52] Mark: Timeline: We want a 6-week pilot with weekly check-ins. After pilot we may consider dedicated if traffic economics justify.

[08:02] Priya: Sounds good. For the pilot we'll propose scoped configuration: hosted API, a small reserved burst pool for predictable throughput, pre-selected model variant (quantized cross-encoder), and a benchmark plan.

[08:18] (Priya pulls up benchmark template)

[08:24] Priya: Benchmark notes: we'll run 1k queries with realistic top-K sizes, measure end-to-end latency including vector DB lookup (we can simulate client DB if you prefer), and compare rerank top-k precision metrics.

[08:40] Ravi: Our vector DB is Pinecone; will that integrate smoothly?

[08:45] Priya: Yes — most vector DBs are compatible. We typically run retrieval on your DB and call Redwood rerank as a scoring service. If you want, we can demo with Pinecone in the notebook.

[08:58] Sam: Any chance of running a small A/B where half traffic goes to our current ranker and half to Redwood for live CTR measurement?

[09:06] Alex: Absolutely — we recommend an A/B approach to measure production impact. Console supports rollout rules and traffic splitting per route.

[09:18] Mark: About cost modeling — can you show per-100k queries estimate?

[09:24] Alex: I'll send a one-pager pricing for hosted pilot, including token-based compute for embeddings + rerank calls. For high volume the Dedicated model or reserved capacity may be cheaper. The rough back-of-envelope for your 1.5M/day is in the follow-up.

[09:38] Priya: Quick demo of Optimize suggestions — it scanned sample latency and token patterns and suggested switching to a 4-bit cross-encoder and enabling a 40ms batching window for rerank to improve throughput while keeping p50 acceptable.

[09:56] Lina: Does that batching window increase latency for single queries? We have many low-volume high-value queries during purchases.

[10:03] Priya: Batching introduces tradeoffs. We recommend dynamic batching: low-latency passthrough for priority routes, batching for lower-priority or bulk endpoints. Optimize suggests per-route batching config.

[10:20] Mark: Any references to customers similar to us? Retail with SKUs?

[10:25] Alex: We can share anonymized case studies — we've worked with a couple of e-commerce customers on SKUs and product search. I'll include those links.

[10:34] (short silence)

[10:40] Priya: Last part: security and compliance checklist — SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS, audit logs, region pinning and data export controls. For Private we can run in your VPC if you need air-gapped.

[10:55] Sam: Great. Does Private support our on-prem HSM?

[10:59] Priya: Yes — Private can integrate with on-prem HSMs and KMS. That typically moves into an enterprise procurement track.

[11:08] Mark: Ok, let's talk pilot acceptance criteria: CTR uplift, latency, and a stability factor. We'll write the acceptance criteria and share.

[11:17] Alex: Perfect. We'll draft a 6-week pilot SOW with milestones: week 0 infra setup + data sample; week 1 pilot deploy + sanity tests; week 2 benchmark run; weeks 3–5 live A/B and tuning; week 6 wrap and decision.

[11:34] Priya: Action items recap: Priya will run a hosted bench with your sample; Alex will send pricing, SOW, SOC2 + KMS docs; Mark will share query sample and stakeholders.

[11:48] Mark: Sounds good. One more quick question — are there any rate limits we should be aware of for hosted during pilot?

[11:55] Alex: Hosted has default rate limits per account, but for pilots we can raise caps or provide burst capacity. We'll note that in the SOW.

[12:06] Lina: Thanks everyone.

[12:09] (meeting closing)

Summary (auto): Demo of hosted embeddings + rerank flow, Console/Optimize feature tour, security/compliance discussion (SOC2, SSO, KMS, RBAC), pilot plan for 6 weeks with A/B and benchmark.

Questions noted: latency SLOs vs batching tradeoffs, data residency, Pinecone integration, cost estimates for 1.5M q/day.

Action items (auto): Priya to run benchmark, Alex to send pricing and compliance docs, Mark to share sample queries.

End of transcript.
